# Skein — full LLM context

Skein is a tiny HTML-first Web Components runtime for creative websites and interactive documents. It adds fine-grained reactivity, scoped lifecycle, keyed lists, conditions and ergonomic bindings while leaving rendering media native: HTML stays HTML, CSS stays CSS, SVG stays SVG, and Canvas stays imperative Canvas.

Current public runtime version: 0.3.x.
Canonical browser entry: `skein.js`.
Repository: https://github.com/Pom4H/web-component
Website: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/
Playground: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/playground/

## Core philosophy

1. The browser is already the rendering engine. Do not introduce a virtual DOM.
2. Static content should remain static HTML. Skein binds only dynamic data.
3. SEO-critical content such as the value proposition, headings, links, product copy and structured information should normally be present in the original HTML response. Skein can enhance interactive regions around it.
4. Skein currently has no SSR or hydration. Do not pretend otherwise. If server-computed HTML is required, generate that HTML outside Skein and let Skein enhance the resulting document.
5. Templates should stay readable as HTML. Expressions inside `{...}` are property paths, not arbitrary JavaScript expressions.
6. Put derived logic in `computed()` rather than embedding logic into markup.
7. Prefer native browser APIs over framework abstractions when the platform already provides the capability.
8. Keep the dependency count at zero in the core and examples unless a user explicitly chooses otherwise.

## Smallest app

```html
<!doctype html>

<click-count></click-count>

<template skein="click-count">
  <script>
    this.count = 0
    this.up = () => this.count++
  </script>

  <button @click={up}>clicked {count}</button>
</template>

<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Pom4H/web-component@main/skein.js">
</script>
```

No npm, CLI, bundler, config file or dev server is required.

For reproducible production deployments, pin a commit SHA instead of `@main`.

## Larger project convention

A custom-element tag maps to an HTML component file by replacing hyphens with slashes:

```text
<counter-app> -> counter/app.html
<user-card>   -> user/card.html
```

A component file may contain `<script>`, markup and `<style>` in one file.

```html
<script>
  this.name = 'Ada'
  this.greeting = computed(() => `Hello ${this.name}`)
</script>

<h2>{greeting}</h2>

<style>
  h2 { text-wrap: balance; }
</style>
```

## State

Component scripts execute with `this` bound to a deep reactive Proxy.

```js
this.count = 0
this.count++
this.user = { name: 'Ada' }
this.user.name = 'Grace'
this.items = []
this.items.push({ id: 1, title: 'One' })
```

Application code should use normal JavaScript assignments. Do not expose `.get()` / `.set()` signal ceremony unless using low-level runtime primitives intentionally.

## Bindings

Text:

```html
<h1>Hello {user.name}</h1>
```

String attribute:

```html
<div title="User {user.name}"></div>
```

DOM property:

```html
<input .value={user.name}>
```

Boolean attribute:

```html
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
```

Event:

```html
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
<button onclick={save}>Save</button>
```

Legacy inline browser handlers are supported when useful:

```html
<button onpointermove="$.move(event)">Move</button>
```

Every rendered element exposes component state as `$` for this compatibility style.

Context:

```html
<address in={user.address}>
  {city}, {street}
</address>
```

`in={...}` creates a lexical binding context. Lookup walks outward through parent contexts and then component state. An existing local property with value `undefined` still shadows an outer property of the same name.

## Lists

```html
<article for={projects} key={id}>
  <b>{index}. {title}</b>
  <input placeholder="DOM state survives reorder">
</article>
```

Use a stable `key={id}` when records have application identity.

Without an explicit key:
- objects use object identity;
- primitive duplicates are disambiguated by occurrence.

List reconciliation is incremental:
- append creates only new views;
- removal disposes only removed views;
- reorder moves existing DOM nodes instead of recreating them;
- local DOM state such as input value can survive reorders;
- `index` and `$index` are reactive list locals.

Do not replace keyed lists with full `innerHTML` rerenders.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={inspectorOpen}>
  <canvas></canvas>
</section>
```

A conditional branch owns a child reactive scope. When it becomes false, its effects, event listeners, nested scopes and DOM range are disposed together.

## Computed values

```html
<script>
  this.price = 100
  this.quantity = 2
  this.total = computed(() => this.price * this.quantity)
</script>

<strong>{total}</strong>
```

`computed()` values are lazy, cached and dependency-tracked.

Use computed values for derived presentation state instead of putting arithmetic or arbitrary expressions in template braces.

## Effects and scheduling

```js
effect(() => {
  console.log(this.total)
})
```

Synchronous state writes are batched into a microtask. Render effects settle before user effects.

```js
batch(() => {
  this.x = 1
  this.y = 2
})
```

Use `untrack(fn)` when a reactive value must be read without creating a dependency.

## Lifecycle and cleanup

Every component owns a root `Scope`. Lists and conditional branches create child scopes.

Prefer native `AbortSignal` integration:

```html
<script>
  window.addEventListener('resize', this.measure, { signal: abortSignal })
  fetch('/data.json', { signal: abortSignal })
</script>
```

For resources without AbortSignal support:

```js
const timer = setInterval(this.tick, 1000)
onCleanup(() => clearInterval(timer))
```

`disconnectedCallback()` pauses a component rather than permanently destroying it. Reconnection resumes dirty bindings. `connectedMoveCallback()` is supported for state-preserving custom-element moves.

Permanent teardown is explicit:

```js
component.dispose()
```

## SEO and progressive enhancement

Skein currently has no SSR. This does not mean all page content must be client-rendered.

Recommended content-first page:

```html
<main>
  <h1>Creative websites with native HTML, CSS, SVG and Canvas.</h1>
  <p>Skein adds fine-grained reactive bindings without a virtual DOM or build step.</p>
  <a href="/pricing/">See pricing</a>

  <price-calculator></price-calculator>
</main>
```

The heading, paragraph and link are already present in the HTML response. Skein owns the interactive calculator.

When generating a Skein site, do not hide meaningful static content inside a component only because the framework exists. Use Web Components as interactive islands unless encapsulation is genuinely useful.

If the server must compute personalized or request-dependent HTML before delivery, use an external server/static-generation layer. Skein can enhance that HTML after delivery.

## Creative CSS pattern

Bind state into attributes or CSS custom properties and let CSS animate/layout:

```html
<script>
  this.x = 50
  this.move = event => this.x = event.offsetX
</script>

<article style="--x:{x}px" @pointermove={move}>
  <h1>Skein</h1>
</article>

<style>
  h1 { transform: translateX(var(--x)); }
</style>
```

Do not reproduce CSS interpolation, transitions, layout or keyframes in JavaScript unless necessary.

## SVG pattern

Keep the SVG tree native and bind only dynamic attributes:

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <circle cx={x} cy={y} r="4" />
</svg>
```

Use CSS and SVG features directly. Do not convert SVG into a framework-specific object tree.

## Canvas pattern

Canvas should normally retain an imperative render loop. Skein should manage state, controls, ownership and cleanup rather than trying to make each pixel declarative.

```html
<script>
  this.speed = 1

  const ctx = host.shadowRoot.querySelector('canvas')?.getContext('2d')
  let frame

  const draw = () => {
    // ordinary canvas rendering using reactive state
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(draw)
  }

  frame = requestAnimationFrame(draw)
  onCleanup(() => cancelAnimationFrame(frame))
</script>
```

When DOM availability timing matters, initialize the loop after the relevant node exists or bind setup to an appropriate lifecycle point.

## Public helpers inside component scripts

- `computed(fn)` — lazy cached derived value.
- `effect(fn)` — user effect scheduled after render work.
- `onCleanup(fn)` — register deterministic teardown.
- `batch(fn)` — group synchronous writes.
- `signal(value)` — explicit low-level signal ref.
- `untrack(fn)` — non-reactive read.
- `host` — current custom-element instance.
- `abortSignal` — current scope-owned AbortSignal.

## Public global/module API

The canonical module exports `Skein`.

Useful surface:

```js
Skein.name
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
Skein.element(tag)
Skein.stats
Skein.flush()
Skein.Signal
Skein.Computed
Skein.Effect
Skein.ReactiveState
Skein.Scope
```

`Skein.define(tag, source)` registers component source directly and is used by the playground.

`window.Skein` is also exposed in the browser.

`web-component.js` exists as a compatibility alias; new documentation and CDN usage should prefer `skein.js`.

## Runtime architecture

Core files:

```text
skein.js
runtime/reactive.js
runtime/template.js
runtime/component.js
```

`runtime/reactive.js` contains signals, computed refs, effects, batching, ownership scopes, the reactive Proxy and lexical BindingScope.

`runtime/template.js` compiles DOM templates once and creates specialized DOM parts including text, attributes, properties, booleans, events, lists and branches.

`runtime/component.js` implements Custom Element loading, component source compilation, lifecycle, helpers, registration and runtime exports.

Runtime invariants:
- no virtual DOM;
- no component-level rerender loop;
- templates compile once per component source;
- exact reactive reads drive exact parts;
- DOM parts skip identical commits;
- keyed list identity must be preserved;
- scopes own effects and cleanup;
- render work runs before user effects;
- no core third-party dependency.

## Testing

Run the project test suite with:

```bash
node test/run.mjs
```

Requirements:
- Node.js 22+;
- Chrome or Chromium, or `CHROME_BIN=/path/to/chrome`.

The runner uses Node built-ins and Chrome DevTools Protocol directly. Do not add Playwright, Puppeteer, jsdom, Jest, Vitest or another test dependency merely to test core runtime behavior.

Tests cover reactive core behavior, browser bindings, keyed identity, reorder/disposal, scheduler batching, lifecycle/reconnect, creative examples, Skein bootstrap APIs, a 1000-row performance smoke test and legacy compatibility.

## Current limitations

- no SSR or hydration;
- no built-in async resource/suspense primitive;
- no built-in error-boundary component primitive;
- `{...}` expressions are property paths rather than arbitrary JavaScript;
- component scripts currently use `AsyncFunction`, so strict CSP requires an `unsafe-eval` allowance.

Do not silently claim these features exist. Design around them explicitly.

## Rules for AI agents

When asked to create a Skein application:
1. Start with the smallest native HTML solution that satisfies the request.
2. Keep semantic and SEO-critical content outside dynamic components when it can be static.
3. Add Skein components only where interactivity/state is useful.
4. Prefer one-file `<template skein>` for tiny examples and prototypes.
5. Prefer external `tag/name.html` component files for larger projects.
6. Keep `{...}` bindings to paths; use `computed()` for derivation.
7. Use `.property`, `?boolean`, and `@event` bindings with their intended DOM semantics.
8. Use stable keys for persistent list identity.
9. Use CSS for visual state and animation whenever possible.
10. Use native SVG and Canvas APIs directly.
11. Register cleanup with `abortSignal` or `onCleanup()`.
12. Do not add a framework, state library, templating library or editor library unless the user explicitly requests one.

When asked to modify the Skein runtime itself, read the repository `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/skein/references/architecture.md`, relevant runtime source and tests before changing behavior.
